what_happened: Traced every live caller of the implement-postflight status transition and found two structurally independent call sites (skill_postflight_update vs. reconcile-task-status.sh's direct update-task-status.sh calls), plus a related pre-existing gap: reconcile-task-status.sh never calls skill_orchestrate_propagate_completion, so completion_summary/roadmap_items are not back-filled on the deferred path either. This surfaced early via direct grep tracing rather than after a design was already committed to a single call site.

Carried-figure check: the research report cites skill_orchestrate_propagate_completion at skill-base.sh:1083; its live definition is at skill-base.sh:1746. Every other file:line figure in the report (skill_postflight_update:1010, skill_propagate_memory_candidates:1223, skill_propagate_completion_summary:1313, orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh:1439/1442, reconcile-task-status.sh:656/684/695 and 699/734/742) verified exact. Corrected in the plan rather than carried forward.

The generated dispatch file's Issue Log section states a '15-class seed enum' for issue-record.sh --class; both context/formats/issue-log.md and issue-record.sh's own ISSUE_SEED_CLASSES array carry 16 classes. Stale figure in the dispatch template (orchestrate-build-dispatch.sh), outside this task's scope -- recorded rather than fixed.

The research report's central structural finding -- that reconcile-task-status.sh's implementing)/partial) promotion arms call update-task-status.sh postflight directly, bypassing skill_postflight_update and every propagation helper -- verified exactly as reported on first grep, including the zero-live-caller status of skill_propagate_memory_candidates. The report's explicit two-call-site warning removed the single most likely design error from this plan at zero planning cost.
